brief: A color palette generator that works like a musical instrument — play colors, harmonies lock like chords

dominant_strengths: Clean dark-mode shell with legible sans-serif headers and tidy keyboard-shortcut affordances on the right rail
Saturated 12-step hue row reads as a clear chromatic 'keyboard,' supporting the musical-instrument metaphor at a glance
dominant_weaknesses: Vast empty canvas above and below the swatch row wastes 70% of the screen and breaks compositional balance
The 'musical instrument' brief is undelivered — no staff, chord visualization, harmony arcs, or tonal feedback shown in static state
Color Values and Current Harmony panels are empty placeholders, leaving the interface feeling like a wireframe rather than a finished product
fix_priorities: Visualize harmony as connected arcs/chords across the hue wheel or keyboard so 'locking' feels musical and spatial
Populate Color Values and Current Harmony with live HEX/HSL data and a chord-name analogy to fulfill the metaphor
Recompose layout — center the keyboard vertically, add a hue wheel above, and reduce the dead negative space
Introduce subtle motion/glow on key press to convey the instrument-like responsiveness implied by the brief
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral is moderate from saturated swatches, but behavioral feedback is weak and reflective payoff is missing because the harmony metaphor never manifests visually.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — the keyboard-row metaphor is legible, but without harmony visualization or chord-locking feedback the instrument concept stays conceptual rather than felt.
